prospect.name: Nick
prospect.location: United States (mortgage, 401k, daycare); city not stated
prospect.occupation: Software designer, works from home, roughly 9:00-17:30
prospect.family_status: Married; one young daughter in daycare
prospect.training_background: Trained a few days a week before his daughter was born, now mostly fallen off; bought kettlebells around her birth; previously bought a guided kettlebell course (Gabe West) and abandoned it; used to go to a gym; keen gardener and does heavy yard work; describes himself as having been 'the skinnier person' his whole life
prospect.medical: Recurrent ankle injuries from skateboarding in his teens and early twenties plus a soccer injury about ten years ago, leaving restricted dorsiflexion on the right side - 'not able to get as deep into a squat as I can on like the right side'. Tight hips and intermittent back stiffness from sitting. No conditions disclosed.

signals: Had good routines pre-child and lost them - 'I think I've just gotten away from that'
Turning 40 and reading about middle-age habits setting up the long term
Wants to prove to himself he can still do it - 'it's always been like a more of a maintenance... but I think it's like getting harder and harder now'
Not in a crisis and not chasing marginal gains; recovering a former standard

goals.text: Get back on track with health before 40 because habits set in middle age carry long term
Be around for his daughter and any future grandchildren - 'I don't want to be the dad that dies at 50 from a heart attack'
Lose a few pounds and look more cut
Put on some muscle mass having been skinny his whole life
Improve ankle and hip mobility so everything feels good while training
Prove to himself that he can still do it

Restricted right-ankle dorsiflexion limits squat depth; tight hips and back stiffness from sitting

objections.raw_quote: That might be a little out of my range. Yeah, I don't know if I can swing that right now. I'd have to talk with my wife around budgeting.
objections.rep_response: Split the objection cleanly - asked whether the money simply is not there or could be found - then parked it, delivered the full three-pillar pitch, and came back to it with a full open-wallet sequence.

objections.raw_quote: I know we talked a little bit about 20, like, if I needed a little bit of time to save up for something like this, is it, oh, is it something I can sign up for, assuming I'm a fit for the program, is it something I could be, in a month or two from now, be like, OK, now that I have everything good to go, I can sign up now, yeah.
objections.rep_response: 'Yeah, we can come back to the subject. However, if, like, let me ask you this, how do you feel actually about this? If you had the money right now, would you be open to actually roll in?' Then moved to structure something now rather than in two months.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I need to talk with my wife about this a little bit, just to make sure we're on the same page.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it, de-pressurised - 'I don't want you to commit to anything, man' - and booked a Monday follow-up. None of the OB moves ran.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I think I'd rather save it up, and then have it ready to spend, versus taking the debt to pay for it, I guess.
objections.rep_response: 'It's up to you, man. We can check it out. You don't have to go for it, but just check the option, and how much is it, and then you will decide.' Sent the financing link anyway.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No in-house plan structured. Rep proposed third-party financing (named Affirm or Klarna) spread over up to 12 months, with the interest rate explicitly unknown - 'I cannot say what's going to be the interest rate, because it differs from client to client' - and sent a link so the prospect could see his own quote.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: it's a six-month transformation, yeah? So that's the baseline that we're talking about, and that comes with a guarantee.

evidence: No payment, no deposit, no commitment - 'I need to talk with my wife about this a little bit, just to make sure we're on the same page'
Explicit next call agreed: 'It's Friday. Let me get back to you on Monday. We have like a full weekend, so you can talk it over, check the finances, and I'll call you like during the day on Monday'
Intent is genuine - 'the accountability is, like, the big one that's really interesting to me... it's just finding the money, I think'
Counter-evidence on likelihood: $1,500 available and roughly $400/month surplus against a $6,000 price, and he explicitly prefers saving up to financing
outcome.next_step: Rep to call Monday after the prospect reviews the financing quote and speaks with his wife.

notable.note: The most thorough open-wallet in the batch and the most uncomfortable. The prospect disclosed $1,500 cash, roughly $400 a month spare, a 401k he cannot touch, and that credit cards frighten him because he has been in trouble with them before. The rep's next move was to propose 12-month third-party financing at an interest rate he could not state, and to send the link after the prospect said he would rather save up than take on debt. The rep also told him the company rejects roughly 70% of applicants - the same line he used on the 06/11 call - while the internal close-rate KPI is 25%.
